evidence: Receiving DO2 drops from 11.52 mg/L at t=48.0 to 4.40 mg/L at t=48.2 and declines monotonically to 3.27 mg/L at t=52.0 (decision time)
Linear fit of receiving DO2 over t=48.2-52.0 gives slope -0.257 mg/L/h, projecting ~2.5 mg/L by t=56 and breach of the 2.0 mg/L minimum by t~58 under KEEP
Receiving P assay: 0.0 g/L at t=24, 1.15 g/L at t=36, 3.27 g/L at t=48 - active productive metabolism driving oxygen demand
Source batches (source-1/2/3) never show DO2 below ~7.4 mg/L after their benign t=24-28 dip; receiving's persistent low-DO excursion is anomalous
allowed_actions: increase_air = [1.0, 1.15] (feed unchanged); reduce_feed options sacrifice 20-40% feed-driven production
args.rationale: Receiving DO2 shows an anomalous sustained decline (11.5 -> 4.4 mg/L abrupt drop at t=48.2, then ~-0.26 mg/L/h) toward the 2.0 mg/L minimum, with projected breach by ~t=58 under KEEP. Active product accumulation (3.27 g/L at t=48) confirms real oxygen demand. increase_air (1.15x) adds oxygen-transfer capacity without any feed cut, retaining full product mass — the least-destructive intervention that addresses the oxygen constraint. Feed reduction is held as escalation if DO does not stabilize.
args.uncertainty: Air scale factors and OUR/OTR parameters are hidden; the 1.15x increase may be insufficient to reverse the decline if demand keeps growing (DO headroom at decision time is only ~1.3 mg/L). If DO continues falling below ~3 mg/L after intervention, escalation to combined (0.8x feed + 1.15x air) would be justified. The delayed product assays (4 h turnaround) also mean current true P/DO state estimates carry lag uncertainty.
